title: U.S. House · Texas's 16th District
area: El Paso and surrounding El Paso County, in far West Texas.

context.text: Incumbent Veronica Escobar (D) ran unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary. Adam Bauman won the Republican nomination in a May 26, 2026 primary runoff, defeating Manuel Barraza.

candidates.name: Veronica Escobar

summary.text: Veronica Escobar is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Texas's 16th District. A third-generation El Pasoan, she taught English, ran a nonprofit, and served as El Paso County Commissioner and County Judge before winning the seat in 2018. She serves on the House Appropriations and Budget committees in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

background.text: Born in El Paso, Texas, in 1969. Her official biography describes her as a third-generation El Pasoan.
Graduated from the University of Texas at El Paso and New York University; Ballotpedia lists a bachelor's degree in 1991 and a master's degree in English Literature in 1993.

Before elected office, taught English at the University of Texas at El Paso and El Paso Community College, served as communications director for former El Paso Mayor Raymond Caballero, and was executive director of Community Scholars, a nonprofit that taught high school students to produce public policy reports.

Served as an El Paso County Commissioner from 2006 to 2010 and as El Paso County Judge from 2011 to 2017. Her official biography says she worked with University Medical Center of El Paso to build primary care clinics and the El Paso Children's Hospital.

Won the Democratic primary and the November 6, 2018 general election for the open seat previously held by Beto O'Rourke, defeating Republican Rick Seeberger; took office in 2019. Her official biography says she was the first woman elected to represent El Paso in Congress.

In earlier terms she served on the House Judiciary, Armed Services, and Ethics committees; she now serves on Appropriations (with Budget in the 119th Congress). In the 118th Congress she was one of three co-chairs of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee.

Her official biography lists membership in the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Congressional Progressive Caucus, New Democrat Coalition, Democratic Women's Caucus, and Pro-Choice Caucus, and describes her legislative work on immigration, gun safety, health care, and reproductive health clinic security.
According to her official biography, she lives in Central El Paso with her husband, Michael; they have two grown children.

positions.summary: Her official site says healthcare is a right every American should enjoy and lists the Medicare for All Act among legislation she supports.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Escobar believes healthcare is a right every American should enjoy

positions.summary: Her official site lists the Women's Health Protection Act, which would create a federal right to access abortion, among legislation she supports.
Her official site calls universal background checks and an assault weapons ban a top priority and lists her cosponsorship of the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025.
positions.quote: Common-sense gun violence prevention, such as requiring universal background checks and banning assault weapons, has been a top priority for Congresswoman Escobar.

positions.summary: Her official site says tax policy should prioritize working families and small businesses rather than billionaires and corporations, and cites her support for the Inflation Reduction Act, which it says holds corporations accountable to pay their fair share of taxes.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Escobar believes tax policies should prioritize working families and small businesses, not billionaires and corporations.

positions.summary: Her official site lists the Raise the Wage Act, which would gradually raise the minimum wage to $17 by 2030, among legislation she supports.
Her official site says she will continue to support a transition to a clean energy future and cites her role in passing the Inflation Reduction Act's clean-energy investments.
positions.quote: I will continue to support our transition to a clean energy future

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (Subcommittee on Homeland Security; Subcommittee on Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies) and the Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Adam Bauman
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff over Manuel Barraza.

summary.text: Adam Bauman is the Republican nominee challenging Escobar. A U.S. Navy Special Warfare Combatant Crewman veteran who also served in the U.S. Border Patrol's BORTAC tactical team, he lists his profession as business owner. His campaign website emphasizes lower property taxes, border security, and veterans' issues.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Navy as a Special Warfare Combatant Crewman (SWCC), according to his campaign website and Ballotpedia.
Worked with the U.S. Border Patrol as a member of the Border Patrol Tactical Team (BORTAC); his campaign website describes this as a career in the Border Patrol.
Lists his profession as business owner on Ballotpedia.
Advanced from the March 3, 2026 Republican primary to a runoff and won the May 26, 2026 runoff over Manuel Barraza to become the nominee.

priorities.text: Lowering El Paso property taxes, which he says are among the highest in Texas.
Supporting Customs and Border Protection's mission to secure the border.
Expanding care and benefits for military veterans.

positions.summary: His campaign website says he is committed to women-only sports, in the wording quoted here.
positions.quote: Biological men have no business competing in women's sports
